newsitem.title: USA: GM schedules overtime at truck plants.
newsitem.headline: GM schedules overtime at truck plants.

text.p: General Motors Corp, hit with a strike at one of its three full-size pickup truck plants, said Thursday it has scheduled overtime next week at the remaining two truck plants in North America.
Daily overtime is scheduled for the Fort Wayne, Ind., pickup truck plant and Saturday overtime is slated for the truck plant in Oshawa, Ontario.

Fort Wayne builds regular cab Chevrolet C/K and GMC Sierra pickups. Oshawa builds extended cab versions. GM's Pontiac East plant, where workers went on strike early April 23, is the only other plant that builds extended cab pickups.
GM has also scheduled overtime for its Janesville, Wis., truck plants, and one week of downtime at its Shreveport, La., compact pickup truck plant.
For its car production, GM plans Saturday overtime at the Bowling Green, Ky., Corvette plant, and Oshawa facility that makes the Chevrolet Lumina and Monte Carlo, and Buick Regal and Century.

Ford Motor Co said its Lorain, Ohio, car plant will be idled for two weeks starting April 28 because of a shortage of orders for the Ford Thunderbird and Mercury Cougar coupes. The plant normally makes about 3,200 units a week. About 1,800 workers are affected.
Ford said several of its light truck operations are working daily and Saturday overtime this week.
Chrysler Corp, also hit with a strike, said four of its nine U.S. assembly plants and two of its three Canadian assembly plants will operate the week of April 28.
